summary: This is a Snowflake documentation reference page for the ST_DWITHIN geospatial function. It explains that ST_DWITHIN returns TRUE when the minimum geodesic distance between two GEOGRAPHY values is within a given distance in meters, and FALSE otherwise. It gives the syntax, argument types, a NULL-handling usage note, and a worked example using points one degree apart on the equator.
one_line: Snowflake reference for ST_DWITHIN, which tests whether two geography values lie within a specified distance in meters.
key_facts: ST_DWITHIN returns TRUE if the minimum geodesic distance between two points is within the specified distance, otherwise FALSE.
For GEOGRAPHY values that are not points, such as lines or polygons, ST_DWITHIN uses the minimum geodesic distance between the two closest points of the two values.
The first two arguments must be expressions of type GEOGRAPHY.
The distance_in_meters argument must be an expression of type REAL and is measured in meters.
ST_DWITHIN returns NULL if any input is NULL.
The page tip says the search optimization service can improve the performance of queries that call this function.
The example SELECT ST_DWITHIN (ST_MAKEPOINT(0, 0), ST_MAKEPOINT(1, 0), 150000) returns True.
In the example, two points one degree apart along the equator are less than 150,000 meters apart.
